acceptable_changes: Shortened the opening sensory paragraph to keep the length near target.
Compressed the hangman and police exchange into Tommy's single 'cheat the hangman' retort.
Cut the 'listening at that door' questions and the 'How was he to know?' follow-up.
Reduced the 'Dead men tell no tales' run to two lines plus Tommy's racing heart.
Condensed the 'you foreigners' speech but kept Boris's admission and the 'mind reader' aside.
Cut the 'little Conrad' compromise, the 'ounce of tact' complaint, and the 'liberty in my own way' exchange together. Tommy's grumble and acceptance are kept.
Trimmed the descriptions of the room and the stairs. Kept hunger and headache for the next chapter's opening.
review_focus: The jump from Tommy's 'Several' straight to his question, after the cuts in that exchange.
That the four Faust pictures read as neutral description with no hint that anything is hidden.
That the German's curious looks stay unexplained, with no mention of memory loss.
risks: The word count was not measured, so the section budgets are approximate. The bargain section may run long relative to the room description.
Two attribution tags were added for clarity ('the German asked', 'Tommy went on'). Both speakers are source-supported, and neither tag falls inside a verbatim excerpt.
summary: Abridgment of Tommy's waking in the Soho house, his bluff and bargain over the Danvers papers, his demand to see Jane Finn, and his confinement in the windowless Faust room. All eight verbatim excerpts are retained.
